Neither solution is correct, but Solution B is closer.

**A counterexample to both answers.** Split each vertex class into a set A of size an and a set B of size (1−a)n. Take as edges all triples containing at least two vertices of A.

- **No perfect matching for a < 2/3.** A perfect matching has n edges, each containing at least 2 vertices of A, so it needs at least 2n A-vertices. There are only 3an, and 3a < 2 when a < 2/3.
- **Link of a B-vertex.** Any edge through v∈B must have its other two vertices in A. So N_H(v) is the complete bipartite graph K_{an,an}, with ρ = an.
- **Link of an A-vertex.** The link misses only pairs inside B×B. Its quotient matrix gives ρ = n(a+√(4a−3a²))/2, which exceeds an for a<1.

So the minimum link spectral radius is an, and taking a → 2/3⁻ gives counterexamples with ρ → (2/3)n and no perfect matching. Therefore c ≥ 2/3.

**Checking the solutions against this bound:**

- **Solution A** gives c = 1/2 < 2/3, so it is refuted. Its appeal to "known Dirac-threshold results" is also unsupported, since a minimum-degree condition does not directly control the spectral condition.
- **Solution B** gives (√5−1)/2 ≈ 0.618 < 2/3, so it is also refuted. Its golden-ratio construction is asserted without verification.

Since both values fall below the lower bound 2/3, neither is the true constant. Solution B is nonetheless the closer of the two, so it is marginally more likely to be on the right track.

WINNER: B
